name: Town of Ossining
gaps: County code R-80 is not a district in the Town code (§ 200-3 lists R-40, R-30, R-20, R-20A, R-15, R-10, R-7.5, R-5); entry left null - check the Town zoning map for the parcel's actual district
Building coverage definition not found in § 200-53; recorded as plain % of lot
MF entry uses the § 200-22 multiple-dwelling column; one-family houses in MF are permitted as regulated in R-40 (§ 200-16A(1)), so use the R-40 values for a house there
Pool-specific setbacks not found in Ch. 200 (pools count as impervious surface)
Height measured to the mean between eave and ridge for pitched roofs (§ 200-53)

wetlands.summary: Ch. 105: permit for regulated activities in wetlands, water bodies, watercourses and their buffers: 100 ft from water bodies and non-watercourse wetlands, 50 ft from watercourses; minor activities (e.g. short driveway crossings) by Building Inspector permit.

steep_slopes.summary: Ch. 167: regulates slopes of 15%+ with a 10 ft minimum dimension: 15-25% over 13,068 sf, 25-35% over 8,712 sf, 35%+ over 4,356 sf; steepest qualifying class sets the approval authority.

trees.summary: Ch. 183: permit to remove trees of 6 in.+ DBH, ornamental trees of 3 in.+, any tree of 3 in.+ in the perimeter buffer zone (10 ft in R-40/R-30, 5 ft in R-20/R-20A/R-15 and other listed districts), significant trees, or clear-cut more than 10 trees (6 in.+) per lot in 12 months.

stormwater.summary: Ch. 168: Stormwater Management Officer review and SWPPP for land development activity disturbing 1 acre or more (or part of a larger common plan).

adu.summary: § 200-31.2: accessory apartment by ZBA special permit on single-family lots: 300-800 sf habitable and max 33% of the house's habitable floor area, owner-occupied, only in space with a CO for 2+ years.

general.accessory_structures: Accessory buildings may sit in required side/rear yards if max 15 ft high and 10 ft from any lot line, together max 30% of the required yard; not nearer the street than the house (§ 200-25A).
general.pools: No pool-specific setback found; pools count toward impervious surface (§ 200-53).
general.notes: Indian Brook-Croton Gorge Watershed Overlay (Ch. 117) adds rules in mapped areas. A new one- or two-family house need not be set back farther than the average of existing dwellings within 200 ft on each side (§ 200-25D(3)).

R-40.name: One-Family Residence R-40

max_impervious_coverage.note: Impervious surfaces: buildings plus asphalt, concrete, masonry, wood, gravel or paver areas incl. pools, courts, patios, terraces, driveways (§ 200-53); applies to any residentially used or zoned lot; > 100 sf new impervious needs a Building Inspector permit (§ 200-21B)

max_floor_area.note: Max floor area of a one-family residence = 5,000 + (lot area - 43,560) x 0.052521, for all lot sizes (smaller lots get less than 5,000 sf); floor area excludes cellar/basement areas used only for storage or building operation (§ 200-21C, § 200-53)

accessory.notes: Accessory buildings in required side/rear yards: max 15 ft high, 10 ft from any lot line, together max 30% of the required rear or side yard; elsewhere principal-building height rules; not nearer the street than the house (garages may come to 10 ft / 5 ft from the street line on 10-20% / 20%+ slopes with Planning Board approval) (§ 200-25A)

R-40.source: § 200-21 and Schedule of Bulk Regulations for One-Family Residences (200 Attachment 2, Mar 2021)
R-40.notes: Min livable floor area 850 sf. Corner lots need front yards on both streets (§ 200-25B(2)). Lot depth may be 25% less at any point if the average meets the minimum. On streets with < 50 ft right-of-way, the front yard is measured from the street center line plus 25 ft (§ 200-25D(4)). Min 50 ft street frontage (§ 200-25.1).

MF.notes: One-family houses permitted as regulated in R-40 (§ 200-16A(1)); values shown are for multiple dwellings: 4,000 sf per unit plus 1,500 sf per bedroom. Row/attached dwellings: lot width 20, depth 100, front 25, side 50/100 (between buildings and side lot lines only), rear 40. Min livable floor area 450-1,200 sf by unit size. Impervious table (§ 200-21B) applies to residentially zoned lots.
